labelling.labelledBy: Claude (AI), from the source at the pinned commit
labelling.method: Two separate Python scripts (xml.etree and regular expressions, not CodeAtlas code). The Maven script read all 187 pom.xml files outside .git, node_modules and target, took each module's groupId (its own or its parent's) and artifactId, and labelled one depends_on per <dependency> directly under <project> (not dependencyManagement, profiles, plugins or exclusions) that names a module of this repository, with ${project.groupId} resolved; a child also depends on the modules its in-repository parent POMs list, cited at the parent's line. A folder that also holds a package.json is one module named by its package name. The npm script labelled the 5 dependencies between the 8 workspace packages (dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, optionalDependencies). The first comparison disagreed with CodeAtlas on 89 pairs. On reading the POMs, 62 were labeller errors (it took the groupId of an <exclusion>), fixed in the script; 20 were CodeAtlas defects, fixed in CodeAtlas: a folder with both a pom.xml and a package.json dropped its Maven dependencies (15), and dependencies inherited from a parent POM were used for the import check but not recorded as links (5). 7 remain CodeAtlas misses: quarkus/dist and docs/documentation/dist are real Maven modules in folders named dist, which CodeAtlas excludes as build output. The 5 npm dependencies were added after the first comparison, when CodeAtlas reported them. Labels whose module is test code (a test-support path, such as testsuite/ and the *-tests modules; adjudication guide §3) were then removed, leaving 339 of 465; the counts of disagreements above are over all 465. Awaiting founder spot-check (decision D-9).

scope.rule: A Maven module depends on another module of this repository when a <dependency> directly under <project> (any scope) names it by groupId and artifactId, or when an in-repository parent POM's <dependencies> do. An npm workspace package depends on another when its package.json lists it in dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies or optionalDependencies. One relationship per pair; a folder with both files is one module, named by its package.json.

They declare versions or build tooling, not a module dependency.
